questions.question_text: How many hours of pre-license education must a Utah sales agent candidate complete?
questions.explanation: Utah requires 120 classroom hours of salesperson prelicensing education (61-2f-203(1)(d)(i); R162-2f-202a(1)(c)(i)). Broker candidates also complete 120 hours. An 'hour' means 50 minutes of instruction, and no more than eight program hours may be taken in one day.

questions.question_text: A candidate completed pre-license education 14 months ago but has not yet taken the exam. What is the status of their education?
questions.correct_answer: It has expired and must be retaken
distractors: Only the state portion must be retaken
questions.explanation: Both exam components must be passed, and the license application submitted, within 12 months of completing the prelicensing education (R162-2f-202a(3); Pearson VUE Utah handbook). At 14 months the education no longer qualifies and must be retaken.

questions.question_text: What is the minimum age to obtain a real estate sales agent license in Utah?
questions.explanation: An applicant must be at least 18 (R162-2f-201(3)) and hold a high school diploma, a GED, or equivalent education approved by the Commission (R162-2f-201(4)).

questions.question_text: A candidate arrives at the Pearson VUE test center for the Utah sales agent exam. What document must they present from their school?
questions.explanation: Candidates must present the Candidate Education Certifying Document, which is stamped and signed by the approved school, verifying completion of the required 120 hours of pre-license education.

questions.question_text: As part of the Utah licensing process, candidates must submit to a:
questions.explanation: Every new sales agent, associate broker, and principal broker applicant submits fingerprints and consents to a Utah Bureau of Criminal Identification and FBI background check (61-2f-204(1)(d)). Applicants also sign a waiver enrolling their prints in the FBI's Rap Back service, so the Division is notified of later arrests.

questions.question_text: After passing both sections of the Utah licensing exam, a candidate has how long to apply for a license?
questions.explanation: An application for licensure must be submitted within 90 days of achieving passing scores on both examination components (R162-2f-202a(3)(c)). If the 90th day falls on a weekend or holiday, the deadline moves to the next business day.

questions.question_text: A candidate passed the general portion of the exam in January but failed the state portion. They retake and pass the state portion in April. When does the 90-day application clock start?
questions.correct_answer: From the date both portions are passed
distractors: From the first exam attempt date
From the general portion pass date
questions.explanation: The 90-day application clock starts when both components have been passed. Two other clocks apply: a failed component must be retaken and passed within six months of passing the other one, and everything must fall within 12 months of completing the prelicensing education (R162-2f-202a(3)).

questions.question_text: The total time allowed for both sections of the Utah salesperson exam is:
questions.explanation: Candidates get four hours total for both sections. The national/general portion has 80 scored items plus 5 pretest items; the state portion has 50 scored items plus 5-10 pretest items. Scoring is immediate at the Pearson VUE test center.

questions.question_text: What passing score is required on both portions of the Utah salesperson exam?
questions.explanation: Salesperson candidates need a scaled score of 70 on both the general and state portions; broker candidates need 75 on both. A scaled score ranges from 0 to 100 and is neither the raw number correct nor a percentage.

questions.question_text: A candidate completes prelicensing education in March. By when must the exam be passed and the license application submitted?
questions.explanation: Both exam components must be passed and the application filed within 12 months of completing the prelicensing education (R162-2f-202a(3); Pearson VUE Utah handbook). Education finished in March therefore runs out the following March, even though the separate 90-day application window may be shorter.

questions.question_text: Which person is exempt from Utah real estate licensing requirements?
questions.correct_answer: An attorney acting within their practice
distractors: A property owner's friend helping for a fee
A part-time negotiator paid per deal
questions.explanation: 61-2f-202(2)(b) exempts services rendered by an attorney admitted to practice in Utah while performing the attorney's duties as an attorney. Other exemptions include receivers, trustees in bankruptcy, executors, and persons acting under a court order (61-2f-202(2)(c)).

questions.question_text: A court appoints a receiver to sell real property from an estate. Does the receiver need a real estate license?
questions.correct_answer: No, persons acting under court order are exempt
distractors: Yes, all property sellers need a license
Only if they receive a commission
questions.explanation: 61-2f-202(2)(c) exempts a receiver, trustee in bankruptcy, administrator, executor, or an individual acting under order of a court. The exemption is tied to the court's authority, not to the price or the fee.

questions.question_text: A county employee negotiates the purchase of land for a public highway project as part of their official duties. Do they need a license?
questions.correct_answer: No, government employees in official duties are exempt
distractors: Yes, they are performing a real estate act
Only if the purchase exceeds $1 million
Only if they receive extra compensation
questions.explanation: 61-2f-202(2)(f) and (2)(g) exempt Department of Transportation staff and regular salaried employees of a county, city, or town acting on the entity's behalf in acquiring (including by eminent domain), disposing of, leasing, or managing real estate. There is no blanket exemption for all government employees.

questions.question_text: An active member of the Utah State Bar wants to become a sales agent. What advantage do they have?
questions.correct_answer: They may have education requirements waived
distractors: They are automatically licensed as a broker
They skip the state portion of the exam
They receive a discounted exam fee
questions.explanation: R162-2f-202a(1)(c)(ii) lets an applicant evidence current Utah State Bar membership instead of the 120 hours; the Division notes the waived hours on the Candidate Education Certifying Document. The applicant must still pass both exam components and complete the application.

questions.question_text: A neighbor helps sell a friend's property and accepts a $500 gift in appreciation. Under Utah law, this person:
distractors: Is legal if it was a one-time act
questions.explanation: Selling a property for another person for compensation is a licensed act under 61-2f-201(2), and 61-2f-401(5) makes paying an unlicensed person for it unlawful. The only related exception runs the other way: a licensee may give a gift of $250 or less for an unsolicited referral (R162-2f-401b(1)(l)).
